title: Hydraulic Corner Notchers, Fixed & Variable Angle | NovoTech
meta_description: Hydraulic corner notchers that cut a 90° or 30°–140° corner out of sheet to 1/4″ in one stroke: HNM 4F, 6F and 6V with T-slot table and automatic blade gap.
intro: A corner notcher (notching machine) cuts a square or V-shaped corner out of a sheet in one stroke so the four sides fold up into a box, pan, tray or enclosure on the press brake — the hand-cut, hand-ground corner of the sheet-metal shop done in a second. The HNM range: the fixed 90° HNM 4F for 3/16″ and HNM 6F for 1/4″ mild steel with foot-pedal control and a small footprint, and the HNM 6V variable-angle notcher whose blades swing from 30° to 140° on a T-slot table with automatic blade-gap adjustment and four hydraulic hold-downs. Sold with a CSA-approved panel, blades and support from Mississauga, ON.
hero_points: HNM 4F and HNM 6F — fixed 90°, 3/16″ and 1/4″ mild steel, 20 – 25 cuts per minute
HNM 6V — 30° to 140° variable angle, 1/4″ mild steel, automatic blade gap, T-slot table
Stainless to 11 ga; blade lengths 7.8″ to 9.8″

groups.lead: Fixed 90° notchers and the variable-angle HNM 6V.

faq.a: Boxes, pans, trays and enclosures are 90° corners, and the HNM 4F and 6F cut them fastest at 20 – 25 strokes per minute. Hoppers, cones, chutes, duct transitions and any part whose sides are not square need the HNM 6V, whose blades set to any angle from 30° to 140° and whose T-slot table takes stops for repeat positioning.

faq.q: What does automatic blade-gap adjustment do?
faq.a: Shear blades need a gap that grows with the sheet thickness. On the HNM 6V the gap follows the thickness automatically, so the operator changes from 20 ga to 1/4″ without realigning the blades — and the cut edge stays clean on both.

faq.q: Can the notcher cut stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: Yes — 14 ga (HNM 4F) or 11 ga (HNM 6F / 6V) stainless, and aluminum up to the mild-steel capacity. Blades are hardened tool steel and are resharpened and shimmed back to size.

faq.q: Corner notcher or ironworker notching station?
faq.a: The ironworker's rectangular notching station cuts a slot into the edge of bar and plate; the corner notcher cuts the full square corner out of a large sheet laid on its table with a back gauge, at 20 – 30 strokes a minute. Sheet-metal shops that fold boxes daily want the notcher; structural shops are usually served by the ironworker.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
